what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: London to start and carry the risk; raise in one go
sections.para: The insurer for agent behaviour policies can underwrite and carry the risk in London, sell into the US and EU, and raise capital from investors including the Gulf's funds. About £4.35 million runs it for two years; the rest of the money buys cover: £10 million backs up to about £188 million, £50 million up to £1.52 billion.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Eight lines from London to what a raise buys
sections.para: London for underwriting and for carrying the risk; the US through surplus lines; the EU by one registration, second; about £4.35 million to run it; everything above backs cover; £10 million buys about £94 to £188 million of cover; £50 million about £761 million to £1.52 billion.

sections.label: The question, and why it has more than one answer
sections.line: A managing agent, distribution and a balance sheet differ
sections.para: Pricing and selling needs a distribution licence and a carrier's capital; carrying risk needs an insurer's licence and capital against a bad year; distribution needs licences where the customers are. Each is regulated differently, so one company can have more than one home.

sections.label: Start in London
sections.line: Start as a managing agent and coverholder in London
sections.para: Two of today's AI agent covers are written by Lloyd's coverholders, and the Lloyd's Lab's cohort includes an AI risk engine. FCA authorisation takes up to nine months, or the appointed representative route; an intermediary's capital is the higher of £5,000 or 2.5% of income.

sections.label: Sell into the US
sections.line: Reach the US through surplus lines
sections.para: Surplus lines cover risks with no filed form or rate; the market wrote $143.3 billion in 2025, and Harbor's agent cover is issued there. A US managing agent needs state producer licences and a bond of $100,000 to $500,000. A provider's own captive starts at $250,000 in Vermont.

sections.label: The EU, second
sections.line: The EU second: one registration, a cautious supervisor
sections.para: An intermediary registered in one member state works across the EU; software becomes a product on 9 December 2026. EIOPA wrote in June 2026 of weak oversight of MGAs and of reliance on non-EU capacity. A written, deterministic policy should answer those concerns.

sections.label: Carry the risk in London too
sections.line: Carry the risk in London as a UK insurer or at Lloyd's
sections.para: The PRA's mobilisation regime, since December 2024, lets a new insurer start with restrictions for up to twelve months; the floor is £2.4 million. Or capital at Lloyd's behind a syndicate, a short step for a coverholder. An EU carrier can wait for the second market.

sections.label: The Gulf, for capital
sections.line: The Gulf as a source of capital, not a first market
sections.para: The UAE's financial centres are reworking their insurance rules; the ADGM proposes insurers hold 120% of their capital requirement, and DIFC figures were not verified. The region's funds suit the balance-sheet job; selling there can come later.

sections.label: How much it would take
sections.line: What the money buys is cover; raise once for it
sections.para: About £4.35 million runs the company for two years. Every pound above that, at a 5% or 10% shared-failure share, half reinsured, plus 20%, sets the ceiling: £10 million backs £94 to £188 million of cover, £50 million £761 million to £1.52 billion. Decide the cover, then raise for it.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Not advice; my assumptions; premiums are ceilings
sections.para: Not legal, tax or regulatory advice; the model's inputs are assumptions; currencies are approximate; the Gulf figures are thinner; premium figures assume full use of capital; fronting fees and tax are left out.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: The third memo, a research agent, and capital.py
sections.para: From Dinis's memo of 28 October 2026, with the routes and the estimate as his opinion; every source fetched that day or marked secondary; the model and its data file are in the repository.
